summary: Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at Collegium Carolinum (1792–1795), the University of Göttingen (1795–1798), and the University of Helmstedt (~1798–1799). He held a post at Göttingen from ~1807 to 1855.
Carl Gaedicke worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.
Carl Olson works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and also studied under Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Halle-Wittenberg (~1849–1852) and Bonn (~1852–1853) under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber (1849). He held posts at Schulpforta (~1865–1875), Jena (~1875–1903), and Trinity College Dublin as Professor des Sanskrit.

Carl W. Ernst is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1969–1973) and Harvard University (~1973–1981), and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.
Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Groningen from 1908 to 1916 and at Utrecht University from 1917 to 1946.

Carlo Giussani was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) under Giuseppe Bardelli, and later studied under Albrecht Weber (1863) and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Somerville College (~1947–1951) and under Shigeru Gorai (~1961–1963), and served as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge (~1955–1989).

Carmen Dragonetti was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She served as vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1988–2018), with visiting roles at IIBS (1989) and Nyingma Institute (1996).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn by 2001. She has held posts as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and as a fellow at Ruhr University Bochum.

Carol S. Anderson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2004–2009) under David P. Jackson, worked at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (~1985–2000), and was a researcher at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006–2007).
Carola S. Carstens works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg by 2005.

Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and earned her PhD at the University of Michigan (2001) under Nicholas B. Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, later holding posts at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at University College London and under Thomas William Rhys Davids, lectured at the University of Manchester and SOAS, and served as President of the Pali Text Society (~1923–1942).

Caroline Humphrey studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1962–1966) and under Edmund Leach (~1968–1973). She held posts at Scott Polar Research Institute (~1975–1978), King's College (~1978), University of Cambridge (~1978–2010), and University of Michigan (~2002–2003).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990), where she was a Graduate Teaching Associate, and served as Visiting Lecturer at Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.
